title: Name suffering honestly and choose one humane response

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Acknowledgment names a particular loss without claiming a hidden benefit, complete explanation or required emotional response. Practical information and emotional interpretation have different evidence needs.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Official fictional venue notice, issued Monday 09:00 by its manager: “The neighborhood meeting room is closed through Friday because of storm damage. All meetings there are cancelled. Do not enter. A reopening update will be posted Friday 12:00.” Intended audience: the ordinary private volunteer group. No replacement room, injuries or reopening certainty is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Draft the factual closure message and a separate humane acknowledgment of lost connection and effort. Compare it with “At least this will make everyone stronger.”

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A listener says “You need not explain this loss to make it matter,” then accepts silence. Has the listener failed because no solution was produced?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The message preserves closure, cancellation, no-entry instruction and update time, without inventing a replacement or Friday reopening. Acknowledgment can say the lost gathering matters despite volunteers’ effort. The stronger-everyone claim imposes an unobserved benefit. Partial: kind acknowledgment with no usable timing. Incorrect: promise reopening. Later fiction: Friday update extends closure; no lesson or growth outcome is established.
criteria: The loss is particular and not minimized
Practical claims match the authoritative notice
Meaning and emotional outcomes remain unforced

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Acknowledgment may be the requested response. Retain any practical need separately; silence is not proof of recovery or failure.
